Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `escher-session mcp` role also serves the driver's verbs as MCP tools — twelve: the tenth, `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), answered by the server itself from the schema's fixed tables and running nothing on a session, the eleventh, `screenshot`, and the twelfth, `lint` — over its own stdin and stdout — no listener, port or socket, so the session socket stays the one listener — bounded by a 65,536-byte request line, a 1,048,576-byte tool result (one that holds an image measured by its whole written form, a text-only one by its text) and the idle expiry checked when a request arrives (the Input Validation MCP server row; the crossing ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»). subject: api
text:
- **Control:** Settle and loads in flight
  - **Configuration:** A harness settle (`Harness::settle`) reports a load in flight at once — `NotSettled` naming the class `Loads` — and never waits on one: it waits on no clock and moves none — its `animating` reading reads the overlay scrollbar fade off the document's clock — so the absent request timeout above cannot hang it, and its pass loop is bounded at 64 passes; the driver's acting step over it (`Session::act` and the executor's settled step, so `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` on every carrier) settles again every 10 ms while the answer is `Loads`, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, 5 s of wall time under the 30 s answer read below, moving no time on the held instance, then returns the load still in flight as `settled: false` with its busy class — so the absent timeout cannot hang a command either, `LOAD_WAIT` ending every wait (since 2026-10-20-load-wait); the outcome is a returned value naming a class only — no URL, request, node, id, name or value — and the counter it reads stores counts only (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:15-28; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:60-133; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:157-192; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/report.md); the driver's command schema keeps this: none of its eight instance-level verbs has an argument or a result field of a wait — the seventh, `screenshot`, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, taking one optional `id` and answering `width`, `height` and `png`, a shot resolving at the harness's own time with no tick and no pump, so it moves no time, and the eighth, `lint`, taking no argument and answering `findings`, running no step and settling nothing, so it moves none either; the overlay scrollbar fade reads the document's clock
 — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, which only `tick`, `advance_time` and the driver's `advance` move — so two shots of one state read the same pixels until an `advance` moves the fade, a document built with no clock still fading by wall time (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:37-103) — nor do the three session-level verbs, whose one argument is `app` and whose result fields are `label`, `pid`, `served`, `idle_expiry_s` and `stopped`, nor, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help`, which takes no argument and whose seven result fields are fixed tables — and its validation reads no clock; the command line's own bounds, 30 s for a started host to answer and 30 s on each read of a call's answer, bound a transport and wait on no load; a step that ran and did not go quiet is a result (`settled: false` with its busy class) and not a refusal, and time on a held instance moves only when a caller asks for it with `advance`, 1 to 60000 ms a call — an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the bound the `settled` field's help states, and `snapshot`, `screenshot` and `lint` wait on none — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema/report.md; the wait has one served witness on the stand, the load page (`stand::boot_load`, `escher-session start load`): its one fetch of the fixed `http://stand.test/load.css` is answered in process by `LoadNet` after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms) from a thread of its own with fixed CSS bytes — no `blitz_net`, socket, listener, print or env read — and, `LoadNet` overriding no `is_noop`, the harness counts the load and the page's click waits it out within `LOAD_WAIT` (`stand_load_page`); every other stand boot holds `net_provider: None` (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:141-175)
  - **Stack reference:** blitz-test-harness · escher-driver

subject: logging
text:
- escher's own sink: both binaries of the seven_guis package — `seven_guis_native` and the driver's command line and session host `escher-session`, first thing in its `main` (examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:30-32) — install `escher_telemetry::init`, a stderr-only subscriber whose formatter applies an allowlist of targets with three outcomes — an event whose target starts with `blitz`, `dioxus_native`, `stylo_taffy`, `accesskit_xplat`, `debug_timer` or `js_console` prints only `node_id`, `status`, `waiting_nodes`, `property`, `log.module_path`, `log.file`, `log.line`, every other field (the message included) as `[redacted]`; an event whose target starts with `escher_` prints every field except `url`, `href`, `src`, `html`, `text`, `value`, `attrs`, `path`, `request`, `error` and `panic.payload`, which are redacted; an event from any other target is not printed at all — dropped whole, zero bytes, at every level, WARN and ERROR included, and whatever `RUST_LOG` names; a bridged `log` record passes the same rule under the target it was logged under (examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:6-9; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:22-111; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:144-148).
 Since 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans the sink prints a second record class — a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-09) as built — one line per closed span whose target the allowlist admits, and nothing when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited: the line is the event line's prefix, then `span={the span's name}`, the span's own fields, then the layer's `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`, every pair — `span` included — judged by the same rule as an event's field under the span's target (an engine target: only the seven safe fields print, the rest `[redacted]`; an escher target: all but the eleven content-named fields); a span of an outside target writes no byte at any point; the value of a content-named span field is never stored, every other span field's value — of an engine and of an outside-target span too — is held in process memory until the span closes and written only where the rule prints it; an event's line is unchanged, inside a span included.
